about: Pairs of knowledge notes about this repository's own code, labelled by reviewers: `duplicates` say the same thing, `distinct` are other pairs of notes about the same module. Kept notes carry the start of their text only. The default similarity thresholds are checked against them.

entries.title: Allocation replacement requires positive disposal and a durable workspace checkpoint
entries.text: EnvironmentLifecycle._retire_terminal_allocation(reason='replacement') leaves reconnect authority intact unless the workspace-checkpoint record is phase='durable' and the factory's is_allocation_disposed returns the exact bool True. Before retiring, its checkpoint transform rechecks the same reconnect owner and receipt and refuses pending allocation, disposal, or completion-finalization authority; a reconnect exception alone never authorizes replacement.

entries.title: Dynamic-secret terminal workspace deltas are intentionally quarantined
entries.text: Final workspace evidence for dynamic-secret environments is intentionally content-free: _final_workspace_revision_payload replaces arbitrary revision/branch values and finalization deltas with fixed truncated projections, and _final_workspace_snapshot_payload suppresses snapshots. A raw-versus-aliased identity mismatch in _final_workspace_delta_payload therefore does not change the published dynamic-scope delta; detailed delta comparisons apply to static-secret environments.

entries.title: Allocation ownership_epoch is not the session run epoch
entries.text: EnvironmentFactoryRequest.ownership_epoch is intentionally None for ordinary per-session requests (documented in environments/factory.py). It represents a durable allocation claim generation, not Session.run_epoch; shared-allocation request builders populate it from their record's claim_generation. Do not treat its omission from EnvironmentLifecycle.resolve_factory's per-session request as an unimplemented session-epoch forwarding bug.

entries.title: Dynamic final workspace evidence is deliberately quarantined
entries.text: EnvironmentLifecycle builds final workspace payloads through runtime/_final_workspace_payloads.py. For a non-static secret-resolution scope, final revisions and deltas are intentionally content-free/truncated, snapshots and final Git receipts are omitted, and workspace/extension-observer identities are aliased. An inability to match raw final observation identities to aliased tool-window baselines does not by itself lose an intended dynamic finalization delta.

entries.title: Terminal workspace evidence intentionally quarantines dynamic secret scopes
entries.text: EnvironmentLifecycle's terminal workspace evidence uses src/cayu/runtime/_final_workspace_payloads.py: when registered_environment_secret_resolution_scope is not static, final revision/delta data is deliberately content-free and truncated, final snapshots are omitted, and final Git receipts are omitted. This remains intentional even when an individual factory result exposes no vault, because the registered factory secret-scope declaration controls the boundary.

entries.title: Progress reporter reserves the orphan-reconciliation terminal slot
entries.text: RuntimeEnvironmentLifecycleProgressReporter.report reserves the last configured progress-event slot for a terminal event (nonterminal emissions stop at max_progress_events - 1). EnvironmentLifecycle.reconcile_orphaned_progress increments the last nonterminal event_index by one, so normal reporter output cannot overflow EnvironmentLifecycleProgress.event_index's MAX_ENVIRONMENT_PROGRESS_EVENTS bound during orphan reconciliation.

entries.title: Command binding recovery authenticates a strictly older saved binding
entries.text: EnvironmentLifecycle._validate_command_binding_recovery requires the saved command-binding source_run_epoch to be strictly less than the current session.run_epoch, verifies the exact durable allocation/profile/binding record, and checks the live incomplete-recovery claim against the store's clock in transform_checkpoint_with_store_time. This entrance reconstructs a recorded binding through _recover_completion_finalization instead of repeating initial bind/copy-in.

entries.title: Progress reporter reserves its terminal event slot
entries.text: RuntimeEnvironmentLifecycleProgressReporter.report coalesces nonterminal observations once event_count reaches policy.max_progress_events - 1, reserving one slot for finish/deadline terminal evidence. Consequently the lifecycle's orphan-progress reconciliation can increment a reporter-produced nonterminal event_index without exceeding MAX_ENVIRONMENT_PROGRESS_EVENTS.

entries.title: Cancelled completion copy-back is retargeted to interruption
entries.text: Completion-critical finalization cancelled while waiting for SyncBinding staging capacity keeps its exact setup owner and pending_completion_finalization marker. A subsequent interruption terminalization goes through _retarget_retained_completion_finalization, rewriting that marker's outcome from completed to interrupted and changing the owner's retry outcome; tests/core/test_completion_copyback_cancellation.py exercises this transition and restart recovery.

entries.title: Private argument continuity is materialized after both context-build paths
entries.text: ModelStepRun applies runtime._argument_continuity.materialize to both the initial context messages and the context-overflow recovery messages after _build_context completes, before build_request. Consequently context policies and compactors see only public arguments, and only exact calls retained by context selection regain eligible private arguments for the final model request; docs/private-argument-continuity.md documents this audience boundary.

Therefore ModelStepRun._execute_request's initial renewal handlers for BudgetReservationLeaseLost and asyncio.CancelledError cover ordinary backend renewal failures; a missing catch-all there is not a separate storage-error cleanup gap.

entries.title: Observe counting reuses the staged model dispatch and defers notification consumption

entries.title: Observe-mode counting fences disclosure without consuming child notifications
entries.text: For observe-mode token counting with recalled memory, child notifications, or model failover, ModelStepExecutor.run_with_retries prepares the durable model dispatch before counting but passes consume_child_session_notifications=False. LiveModelAttempt reuses that exact dispatch and consumes the notifications at model-provider entry. A counter-only exposure therefore does not consume fresh child results; tests/core/test_child_session_context.py::test_provider_count_exposure_does_not_consume_terminal_child_notification covers closing after counting and resuming.

entries.title: Provider resolution replay distinguishes active fallback from failure settlement
entries.text: RecoveryCoordinator.resolve_provider_operation treats an exact fallback replay as receipt-only once _provider_operation_disposition_execution_started proves the session is RUNNING with the resolution's interaction, current epoch and execution-profile fingerprint. It deliberately does not take over that running fallback; recover_incomplete_session handles abandoned pre-dispatch work. FAIL dispositions still enter finish_pending_provider_operation_disposition after matching durable failure progress so outstanding terminal publication and hook settlement can finish. tests/core/test_provider_operation_offline_recovery.py covers concurrent exact fallback replay and pre-dispatch cancellation/recovery.

entries.text: SessionEngine._reconstruct_targeted_tool_grants intentionally includes expired or revoked durable grant records when preserve_native_projection_snapshot=True, so native provider replay retains the exact historical additional_tools item. This snapshot is not new-use authority: expiry and revocation are enforced separately by the store's atomic use-binding path.

entries.title: Queued-delivery overrides must reattest atomic profile handoff

A subclass overriding that method must redeclare the capability; merely inheriting the version is intentionally insufficient. Fault-injection stores testing successor delivery need that attestation to reach the handoff path.

entries.title: Pausing tools still pass argument-schema admission
entries.text: ToolRoundExecutor.policy_plan calls ToolInvocationAdmission.authorize before selecting a user-input or wake pause. authorize runs _registered_tool_argument_error and returns DENY for invalid registered schemas before calling the tool policy; _first_pausing_tool_call skips DENY outcomes. For supported pausing tools, the prompt selector's lightweight parsing is therefore not the argument-validation boundary.

entries.title: Resolved vault secrets reach the round observer before the tool
entries.text: In dynamic ordinary tool rounds, InvocationVault._resolve_and_publish awaits its on_redactor_change observer before returning a resolved secret. ToolRoundRun supplies DurableToolRound.record_redactor, which merges and persists the cumulative scope through the publication coordinator; cancellation after ctx.vault.resolve returns therefore does not by itself mean the round has lost that resolved secret's redaction scope.

entries.title: Pause selection follows schema-validating policy admission
entries.text: ToolRoundExecutor.policy_plan calls ToolInvocationAdmission.authorize before selecting a pause. authorize validates registered input schemas and returns DENY for invalid arguments; _first_pausing_tool_call requires AUTHORITATIVE policy evidence and skips DENY. Thus malformed built-in ask_user/sleep_until arguments fall through to ordinary rejection, rather than reaching prompt/wake planning as authorized pauses.

entries.title: Executor regression tests enter asyncio through synchronous pytest wrappers
entries.text: Focused executor tests under tests/core use synchronous pytest functions that enter an inner async scenario with asyncio.run (see test_tool_round_executor.py). Match that pattern for new executor regressions: an unmarked native async test is not exercised by this repository's current pytest dependency/setup.

entries.title: MCP admission compares source and registered exposure evidence
entries.text: ToolRoundExecutor's MCP admission builds each authoritative manifest hash from both source-tool evidence and registered exposed-tool contracts. _mcp_manifest_status diffs both dimensions, so changes to registered descriptions, schemas, parallel safety or effect classification are audited even when the source manifest is unchanged. McpManifestBaseline validation recomputes that combined hash; baseline-corruption tests must not assume independently valid SHA-256 fields imply valid baseline evidence.

entries.title: Owned task mutations force READ COMMITTED snapshots
entries.text: PostgresTaskStore._owned_store_connection explicitly starts READ COMMITTED transactions, so ordinary queue/continuation claims and reclamation use fresh snapshots for each post-lock statement even when the database role defaults to REPEATABLE READ. Helpers such as heartbeat that directly use the pool are separate from this owned-connection path.

entries.title: Task-store tests use asyncio.run or the explicit anyio marker
entries.text: Core PostgreSQL tests usually wrap an async scenario in a synchronous test with asyncio.run (for example test_postgres_task_store.py). The async graph/group suites instead set pytestmark=pytest.mark.anyio and provide anyio_backend='asyncio'. A new bare async test without that marker is not run by the repository's locked pytest setup.

entries.title: Continuation page invariants require progress evidence for non-exhausted scans
entries.text: InterruptedTaskContinuationClaimPage validates zero scanned_candidates as necessarily exhausted with no cursor (tasks/handoff.py). A non-exhausted page must have a cursor, so a continuation scan cannot represent 'retry without progress' by merely returning exhausted=False on an empty locked-row batch; it must retain inspection/cursor evidence or perform another bounded selection.

Renewals keep that generation, while a later claim (even with the same worker_id) has a different generation.

entries.title: Explicit bound continuations bypass automated stall throttling
entries.text: The worker helper _run_recovered_interrupted_task_handler serves both generic polling and explicit bound continuations. The Inbox caller in runtime/_inbox_continuation.py and trigger caller in tasks/parked_continuation.py pass apply_unproductive_backoff=False and leave max_unproductive_handoffs=None, so automated stall-history throttling/failure does not apply to these explicit decisions; exact bound claims, session validation, heartbeats and handler settlement still do.

entries.title: Failed busy-slot maintenance still advances its cadence
entries.text: The generic worker's reclaim and fenced-task scans use DurableWorkerCadence.run_if_due, which advances next_run_at in a finally block after every attempted action, including failures. Thus maintained_while_busy logging a failed maintenance pass does not immediately retry in a tight loop; the next attempt remains bounded by reclaim_every_s.
